video.title: Quit Waiting. Start This Simple Business with $0

summary: Chris Koerner and Brandon, owner of an eight-figure marketing agency, trade low-cost growth hacks for local home-service businesses: QR-code 'scan for a prize' yard signs, 'neighbour blitz' door hangers and personalised referral coupons, paying customers to post in local Facebook groups with affiliate links, rock-in-a-bag driveway flyers, writing LLM-friendly blog/FAQ content so ChatGPT surfaces the business, and co-marketing partnerships between non-competing trades. Chris recounts AOL's free-CD campaign (one customer per three CDs, ~$3 CAC for a $50/month customer) as a lesson in riding one channel until ROI turns negative. A key idea: launch a new home service purely by paying high-volume non-competing trades $300 per referred customer.

speakers.name: Brandon
speakers.description: Owner of an eight-figure marketing agency, Utah; returning guest from episode 60

ideas.name: Launch a home service business purely on paid partner referrals
ideas.one_liner: Start e.g. a painting or window cleaning company and pay high-volume non-competing trades (landscapers) $300 per customer they refer.
ideas.business_model: Per-job service; referral fee per customer
ideas.customer: Homeowners already served by partner trades
ideas.problem: New home service businesses need customers fast without ad spend

acquisition_channels.details: Ask a landscaper serving ~50 customers a day to mention you; pay $300 per customer.

quote.text: Hey, would you mind dropping our name to the homeowner and I'll give you $300 for every customer we get?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Owner or crew performs service; website and phone number set up first.

acquisition.how: Partnership deals are human-negotiated; referral tracking can be automated.

uk_applicability.notes: Referral fees between trades are legal in the UK; must be disclosed fairly to consumers.

quotes.text: You can entirely launch it off of this strategy.
quotes.speaker: Brandon

ideas.name: Rock-in-a-bag flyer distribution as a service
ideas.one_liner: Offer driveway rock-and-flyer drops to home service businesses, or launch a higher-ticket home service using only this channel.
ideas.offer: Targeted neighbourhood flyer drops with a rock in an open 4x10 bag

acquisition_channels.details: Driving neighbourhoods tossing bags onto driveways.

ideas.delivery: Assemble rock, flyer, bag and staple at a folding table; throw on driveways.
ideas.startup_cost: About $10 bag of rocks plus flyers

uk_applicability.notes: Unaddressed leafleting is legal in the UK (not covered by PECR), but throwing items onto driveways may raise littering complaints; councils regulate leafleting in some areas.

quotes.text: buy a bag of rocks at Home Depot for 10 bucks, get a bunch of bags.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: He swears that his response rate is like 10 or 20%.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: LLM search optimisation content for local businesses
ideas.one_liner: Write structured blog posts and FAQs designed to be surfaced by ChatGPT answers before competitors do.
ideas.business_model: DIY for owners, or a service
ideas.problem: Customers increasingly search via ChatGPT; competitors haven't optimised
ideas.offer: LLM-friendly content generated with ChatGPT and posted to the website

acquisition_channels.details: Content to be surfaced by LLM search.

ideas.delivery: Prompt ChatGPT to propose topics and write posts; paste on the blog.
unit_economics_claims: ChatGPT-referred YouTube viewers watch ~30% longer (3:54 vs 3:00)

acquisition.how: Selling as a service to UK limited companies can use cold email; sole traders need consent.

quotes.text: Your competitors are not optimizing to be found in the search from Chad GPT. Guaranteed.
quotes.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: QR code 'scan for a prize' yard signs
steps: After a job, place a yard sign with a big QR code and 'Scan for a prize'
Test versions with and without your logo
Capture name, email and phone for a draw (e.g. $100 Amazon card or bundled local gift cards)
Market to the captured leads

quote.text: Have a big old QR code and then a big bold letters. have it say like scan for a prize
quote.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: Neighbour blitz with personalised referral coupons
steps: Bring door hangers and leave them at the ~6 closest neighbours
Give the customer coupons with their name (e.g. 20% off) to hand to neighbours
Use a unique QR/affiliate link per customer to track and reward top referrers

quote.text: you're bringing affiliate marketing to home services.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Pay customers to post in local Facebook groups
steps: Ask happy customers if they're in neighbourhood/moms Facebook groups
Offer a physical $50 Amazon gift card on the spot if they post
Text them a custom link paying $20 per signup; tell them to put the link in the top comment to avoid deboosting
Share a case study of a past payout to motivate
Be willing to sit in the awkward silence when asking

quote.text: there's a lot of money to be made by being willing to sit in the awkwardness.
quote.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: Rock-in-a-bag driveway flyers
steps: Buy rocks (~$10 bag) and open 4x10 bags
Print flyers the same shape as the bag
Assemble rock, flyer, bag, staple
Pick the right neighbourhood per service
Throw on driveways; don't answer calls on day one (mostly angry), answer from day two

quote.text: You don't ever pick up the phone the first day because almost 100% of those first day calls are people that are angry at you
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: LLM-optimised blog content
steps: Prompt ChatGPT: write in-depth blog posts for my site that will rank in LLM search for relevant queries
Let it propose topics, structure and competitor angles
Add your common customer FAQs
Publish on your website

quote.text: Can you write me quality in-depth blog posts for my website that will rank well in LLM searching on chat GPT
quote.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: Co-marketing with non-competing local trades
steps: Find well-rated, similarly sized local businesses that don't compete (roofers and painters, Christmas lights and landscapers)
Meet the owner
Promote each other's services to your customer lists by text and email

quote.text: Why don't more roofers partner with painters? Yes. And just co-arket all the time
quote.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: Book a meeting from a meeting
steps: Never end a sales or account call without the next call booked
End every interaction with a low-friction next step, like ChatGPT asking to continue

quote.text: Book book a meeting from a meeting.
quote.speaker: Brandon

tools_mentioned.name: ChatGPT
tools_mentioned.purpose: Writing LLM-optimised content; LLM search traffic source

warnings.warning: Most business owners don't ask for referrals assertively enough; a throwaway comment doesn't work.

quote.text: 98% of business owners are not nearly aggressive or assertive enough in asking for referrals.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Rock-in-a-bag drops provoke angry calls on the first day.
Low-friction offers increase response but lower intent; specific offers get fewer but better leads.

quote.text: You'll get more scans, you know, lower intent.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Facebook may deboost posts with links; put links in comments.
Paid referral posts in community groups should be disclosed (UK ASA/CMA rules on incentivised endorsements) and referral texts or links must not be sent unsolicited to individuals under PECR.
It's unclear whether ChatGPT's advice on how it ranks content is accurate.

quote.text: how do we know that chat GPT is actually telling us like a method that they actually use to find content on the internet?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Merge offline and online: physical touchpoints (yard signs, coupons) can feed digital funnels and tracking.

quote.text: It's kind of like you're you're merging online and offline.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Test incentive sizes for referrals; after 5-10 tries you'll know whether $20 or $200 is right.
Unusual, non-intrusive formats stand out where standard direct mail is ignored.
Be first on new channels: LLM search traffic is small but higher quality.
Find one channel that works and push it until ROI turns negative, as AOL did with CDs.

quote.text: find the one channel and just beat it to death and still until it has a negative ROI.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Remove friction and always propose the next step to keep customers engaged.
Non-competing businesses serving the same customers can piggyback on each other's trust.
Ads work on everyone at the right moment; timing matters as much as message.

quote.text: no one thinks the ads work for them, but they they work for all of us.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: Growth-hack brainstorm; most tactics are untested ideas, with second-hand numbers (Daniel's response rate, AOL history) and hypothetical referral math.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris promotes TK Owners and his newsletter; Brandon owns a marketing agency.
